physical.physical_description: This rectangular hanging with densely woven decorations is made of silk imported from Vietnam and embellished with silk cocoons to the fringes. Both ends are elaborately decorated with supplementary weft designs in Lao silks including nagas (mythical serpents) and diamond-shaped lanterns. The middle section is decorated in dovetail tapestry technique with numerous images of stylised nagas and two large hybrid creatures called sang hong, the hybrid of an elephant (sang) and an imaginary bird (hong), whose trunks are connected to multi-headed nagas.
physical.summary: Tai weavers often use a multitude of weaving techniques to create a single textile. This densely woven example demonstrates the weaver's mastery of dovetail tapestry and supplementary weft weaving techniques. Some weavers occasionally incorporated tapestry into narrow bands on skirts. Its use as the central portion of this large hanging is a contemporary development.

deep.objectHistory: The application of dovetail tapestry to decorate a large section of a shawl or interior accessory is "new." Small bands of tapestry sometimes were incorporated into skirts by Tai Lue weavers but never into upper body garments, household accessories, or ritual items.
